sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् ।
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥
sentences.tr:
mad-anugrahāya paramam guhyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam |
yat tvayā uktam vacaḥ tena mohaḥ ayam vigataḥ mama ||

morph.gloss: me, my (stem form of aham in compounds)
favor, grace (dat. sg. 'for my favor', i.e. to show me grace)
supreme (sg. neut., agreeing with guhyam and, in the next line, vacaḥ)
secret, mystery (sg. neut., in apposition with vacaḥ 'the word', line 2)
pertaining to the self, the individual self (adhi + ātman; the technical term Kṛṣṇa used and translated 'the individual self' at 8.3)
called, termed, named (past participle of sam-jñā; sg. neut.: 'called adhyātma')
which, that (yat: sg. neut. relative; nom. and acc. are the same form for a neuter)
you (tvayā: instr. sg. 'by you')
to speak (ukta: past participle 'spoken, said', sg. neut.; yat + tvayā stay unchanged in writing, -t + t-; tvayā + ukta- → tvayokta-, -ā + u- → -o-)

delusion, confusion (nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ + a- → -o ' with avagraha marking the lost a-)

to go away, depart (vigata: past participle 'gone, departed', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my')

sentences.l: For my favor, the supreme secret called adhyātma — the word that was spoken by you — by that this delusion of mine is departed.
sentences.i: Out of kindness to me you have spoken the supreme secret teaching known as the individual self; through that teaching this confusion of mine has gone.
sentences.n: Chapter 11 opens with Arjuna speaking, thanking Kṛṣṇa for the teaching just given (chapters 2–10). Guhyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam, 'the secret called adhyātma', names that teaching by the technical term Kṛṣṇa himself used for it (adhyātma, 'pertaining to the self', defined at 8.3 as svabhāva, one's own essential nature, and translated there as 'the individual self' — the same rendering used here in I). The sentence has no separate main verb: paramaṃ guhyam adhyātmasaṃjñitam all describe vacaḥ, 'the word', in apposition — 'the word, [namely] the supreme secret called adhyātma, which was spoken by you'. Two sandhis to notice: tat + śakyam-type -t + ś- patterns recur through the chapter (see v.4), and tvayā + uktam fuses to tvayoktam, -ā + u- → -o-, as at mohaḥ + ayam → moho'yam below (-aḥ + a- → -o with the avagraha marking the lost a-).

sentences.t:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
bhava-apyayau hi bhūtānām śrutau vistaraśaḥ mayā |
tvattaḥ kamala-patra-akṣa māhātmyam api ca avyayam ||

morph.gloss: coming-into-being, origin
passing-away, dissolution (bhavāpyayau: 'origin and dissolution', a dvandva pair-compound, nom. dual masc.; bhava + apyayau → bhavāpyayau, a + a → ā)
indeed, for (particle)
being, creature (gen. pl. 'of beings')
to hear (śruta: past participle 'heard', nom. dual masc., agreeing with bhavāpyayau in a passive sense: 'have been heard')
in detail, at length (adverb from vistara 'extent, detail' + distributive suffix -śas; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mayā: instr. sg. 'by me')
you (tvattaḥ: abl. sg. 'from you', with the emphatic ablative suffix -tas, as in mattaḥ 'from me')
lotus
leaf, petal
eye (kamalapatrākṣa: 'lotus-petal-eyed', vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa; patra + akṣa → patrākṣa, a + a → ā)
greatness, majesty (abstract noun from mahātman; acc. sg. neut.)
also, too
and
imperishable, undiminishing (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with māhātmyam; ca + avyayam → cāvyayam, a + a → ā)

sentences.l: The origin and passing-away indeed of beings have been heard by me in detail, and from you, O lotus-petal-eyed one, your imperishable greatness too.
sentences.i: I have already heard from you, in detail, of the birth and passing of all beings, and of your own greatness that never fades, lotus-eyed one.
sentences.n: Bhavāpyayau, 'origin-and-dissolution', is a dvandva (pair) compound in the dual, its two members glued together as one idea, the coming-to-be and passing-away of all beings — a theme Kṛṣṇa develops throughout chapters 7–10. Kamalapatrākṣa, 'lotus-petal-eyed', is an epithet of Kṛṣṇa; tvattaḥ, 'from you', is the ablative with the emphatic -tas suffix seen also in mattaḥ 'from me'. The second line's verb is understood by ellipsis: '[I have heard] your imperishable greatness too' repeats śrutau from the first line without restating it, a common economy in Sanskrit.

sentences.t:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥
sentences.tr:
evam etat yathā āttha tvam ātmānam parama-īśvara |
draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaram puruṣa-uttama ||

morph.gloss: thus, in this way
this (etat: acc. sg. neut.; final -t before y- written -d, voicing)
as, in the way that
to say (āttha: perfect 2nd sg., an irregular defective-verb form, 'you have said'; etat + yathā → etad yathā, -t + y- → -d y-; yathā + āttha → yathāttha, ā + ā → ā)
you (nom. sg.)
self (ātmānam: acc. sg. 'the self, yourself', object of āttha)
supreme
lord (parameśvara: 'supreme lord', vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa; parama + īśvara → parameśvara, a + ī → e)
to see (draṣṭum: infinitive 'to see')
to wish, desire (icchāmi: present 1st sg. 'I wish')
you (te: enclitic gen. sg. 'your')
form (acc. sg. neut.)
belonging to Īśvara, lordly, majestic, divine (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
person (first compound member)

highest, supreme (puruṣa-uttama, 'highest of persons', rendered 'Supreme Person' wherever it occurs; here vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa; a + u → o. The compound has two senses, and the text does not say which Arjuna means: an honorific, 'best of men', of the kind the epic gives its heroes (Arjuna himself is puruṣarṣabha, 'bull among men', at 2.15), or the title Kṛṣṇa claims for himself at 15.18, the Person beyond the Perishable and the Imperishable. One rendering is kept so that the reader can see it is one word)

sentences.l: So it is, as you have described yourself, O supreme lord; I wish to see your lordly form, O Supreme Person.
sentences.i: It is just as you have described yourself, supreme lord — now I want to see that majestic form, Supreme Person.
sentences.n: Āttha is an irregular perfect ('you have said'), from the defective root ah, which supplies only perfect-tense forms (āha 'he said' appeared throughout chapter 1). Parameśvara and puruṣottama are both vocatives addressed to Kṛṣṇa, 'supreme lord' and 'highest of persons' (rendered 'Supreme Person' wherever it occurs) — titles that anticipate the vision to come. Rūpam aiśvaram, 'the lordly form', uses aiśvara, an adjective from īśvara 'lord', which recurs through the chapter (yogeśvara v.4, mahāyogeśvara v.9, yogam aiśvaram v.8) binding these opening verses together.

sentences.t:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
manyase yadi tat śakyam mayā draṣṭum iti prabho |
yoga-īśvara tataḥ me tvam darśaya ātmānam avyayam ||

if
that, it (tat: acc. sg. neut.; -t + ś- → -c ch-)
possible, able to be done (gerundive of śak; acc. sg. neut.)
I (mayā: instr. sg. 'by me')
to see (draṣṭum: infinitive)
thus (closes the reported thought 'you think that it is possible to be seen by me')
lord, master (vocative sg. 'prabho', the regular vocative form of a u-stem)
yoga
lord (yogeśvara: 'lord of yoga', vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa; yoga + īśvara → yogeśvara, a + ī → e)

I (me: enclitic dat. sg. 'to me')
you (nom. sg.)
to see (darśaya: causative imperative 2nd sg. 'show!'; darśaya + ātmānam → darśayātmānam, a + ā → ā)
self (ātmānam: acc. sg.)

sentences.l: If you think that it can be seen by me, O lord — then, O lord of yoga, show me your imperishable self.
sentences.i: If you think I am able to see it, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, lord of yoga.
sentences.n: Yogeśvara, 'lord of yoga', is Arjuna's climactic address, matched in v.9 when Sañjaya calls Kṛṣṇa mahāyogeśvaraḥ, 'the great lord of yoga', as he reveals the form. Tacchakyam is tat + śakyam, -t + ś- → -cch-, a sandhi that recurs at v.1's tatra note; śakyam is a gerundive, 'able to be done', used impersonally with an instrumental agent (mayā draṣṭum śakyam, 'it is possible for it to be seen by me' — i.e. 'I am able to see it'), the same construction returning as a personal passive in v.8's śakyase.

sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)

to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥
sentences.tr:
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśaḥ atha sahasraśaḥ |
nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇa-ākṛtīni ca ||

morph.gloss: to see (paśya: imperative 2nd sg. 'behold!')
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'my')
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative sg.)
form (acc. pl. neut.)
by the hundreds, hundredfold (adverb; -aḥ + a- → -o ' with avagraha)
and, moreover
by the thousands, thousandfold (adverb)
various, of many kinds
kind, sort (nānāvidhāni: acc. pl. neut., 'of many kinds', agreeing with rūpāṇi)
divine (acc. pl. neut.)
various
color
shape, form (nānāvarṇākṛtīni: acc. pl. neut., 'of many colors and shapes'; varṇa + ākṛtīni → varṇākṛtīni, a + ā → ā)
and

sentences.l: Behold, O son of Pṛthā, my forms, by the hundreds and by the thousands — of many kinds, divine, of many colors and shapes.
sentences.i: Look, Arjuna, at my forms — hundreds of them, thousands of them, of every kind, divine, of every color and shape.
sentences.n: The Blessed Lord now answers, granting Arjuna's request. Śataśas and sahasraśas are distributive adverbs built with the suffix -śas, 'by the hundred', 'by the thousand' — the same formation as vistaraśaḥ in v.2. The compounds nānāvidha and nānāvarṇākṛti, 'of many kinds' and 'of many colors and shapes', both use nānā, 'various', which will recur as aneka, 'many, numerous', through the catalogue of verses 10–11.

पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा ।
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
paśya ādityān vasūn rudrān aśvinau marutaḥ tathā |
bahūni adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi paśya āścaryāṇi bhārata ||

morph.gloss: to see (paśya: imperative 'behold!'; paśya + ādityān → paśyādityān, a + ā → ā)
the Ādityas, a class of solar deities, sons of Aditi (acc. pl.)
the Vasus, eight deities of the natural elements (acc. pl.; final -n before v- stays -n)
the Rudras, eleven fierce storm-deities, forms of Śiva (acc. pl.; final -n before r- stays -n)
the two Aśvins, twin gods of healing and the dawn (acc. dual; final -n before a vowel stays -n and joins directly)
the Maruts, storm-gods, companions of Indra (acc. pl.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
likewise, also
many (bahūni: acc. pl. neut.; -i + a- → -y a-)
not seen before, unprecedented (a- 'not' + dṛṣṭa 'seen', past participle of dṛś, + pūrva 'previous', used adverbially: 'never seen before'; acc. pl. neut.)
to see (paśya: imperative 'behold!'; paśya + āścaryāṇi → paśyāścaryāṇi, a + ā → ā)
wonder, marvel (acc. pl. neut.)
descendant of Bharata (vocative sg.; here addressed to Arjuna)

sentences.l: Behold the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and the Maruts too; behold many wonders never seen before, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: Look at the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and the Maruts as well; behold many marvels never seen before, Bhārata.
sentences.n: A roll-call of Vedic deity-classes: the twelve Ādityas (solar gods), the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twin Aśvins, and the storm-god Maruts — the standard thirty-three gods of the older pantheon, now subsumed into Kṛṣṇa's form. The whole string pañyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau is one written word only because each accusative ends in a consonant that joins directly to the next; the reading separates the five names. Bhārata, 'descendant of Bharata', here addresses Arjuna (in chapter 1 the same title was for Dhṛtarāṣṭra) — both houses descend from Bharata.

sentences.t:
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् ।
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद् द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥
sentences.tr:
iha eka-stham jagat kṛtsnam paśya adya sa-cara-acaram |
mama dehe guḍākeśa yat ca anyat draṣṭum icchasi ||

world, universe (acc. sg. neut.)

to see (paśya: imperative 'behold!')

'thick-haired' or 'conqueror of sleep', Arjuna (vocative sg.)

and

to see (draṣṭum: infinitive)

sentences.l: Here, united in one place, behold today the whole world, moving and unmoving together, in my body, O lord of sleep — and whatever else you wish to see.
sentences.i: Here in my body, Arjuna, see today the whole universe gathered into one place, everything that moves and everything that does not — and whatever else you want to see.
sentences.n: Sacarācaram, 'with the moving and the unmoving', is a standard Sanskrit pair for 'everything animate and inanimate', built from cara 'moving' and its negation acara. Guḍākeśa, 'thick-haired' or, by another reading, 'conqueror of sleep', is the same epithet of Arjuna used at 1.24. Yaccānyad is a triple sandhi worth tracing: yat + ca → yac ca (-t + c- → -c c-), then ca + anyat → cānyat (a + a → ā), and the final -t of anyat surfaces as -d before the voiced d- of draṣṭum that follows.

न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥

na tu mām śakyase draṣṭum anena eva sva-cakṣuṣā |
divyam dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram ||

morph.gloss: not
but
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me')
to be able (śakyase: present passive 2nd sg. of the gerundive śakya, used personally with an infinitive: 'you are able [to see]')
to see (draṣṭum: infinitive)
this (anena: instr. sg. masc. 'with this')
indeed, just, very (anena + eva → anenaiva, a + e → ai)
own

to give (dadāmi: present 1st sg. 'I give')
you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
eye (acc. sg. neut.)
to see (paśya: imperative 'behold!')
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'my')
yoga (here: mystic power, yogic majesty; acc. sg.)
belonging to Īśvara, lordly, majestic, divine (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with yogam)

sentences.l: But you cannot see me with this eye of your own; I give you a divine eye — behold my lordly yoga.
sentences.i: But you cannot see me with your own eyes as they are. I will give you a divine eye — now see my majestic power.
sentences.n: Śakyase is the personal-passive use of the gerundive śak(ya) with an infinitive: not 'you can be seen' but 'you are able [to see]', the construction already used impersonally at v.4. The divya cakṣus, 'divine eye', that Kṛṣṇa now grants is the device that makes the whole vision possible — Arjuna's ordinary sight cannot bear it. Yogam aiśvaram, 'majestic yoga' or 'the yoga-power of lordship', names what Arjuna is about to see: not a static form but Kṛṣṇa's own divine capacity in action.

evam uktvā tataḥ rājan mahā-yoga-īśvaraḥ hariḥ |
darśayām āsa pārthāya paramam rūpam aiśvaram ||

to speak (uktvā: gerund 'having said')
then (-aḥ before r- → -o)
king (vocative sg., Sañjaya addressing Dhṛtarāṣṭra)
great
yoga
lord (mahāyogeśvaraḥ: 'the great lord of yoga', nom. sg., in apposition to hariḥ; yoga + īśvara → yogeśvara, a + ī → e; final -aḥ before h- → -o)

sentences.l: Having thus spoken, then, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed to the son of Pṛthā his supreme lordly form.
sentences.i: Having spoken thus, O King, Hari, the great lord of yoga, then showed Arjuna, son of Pṛthā, his supreme, lordly form.
sentences.n: Sañjaya resumes the narration, addressing the blind king Dhṛtarāṣṭra as rājan, 'O king'. Hari, 'the tawny one', is a name of Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu; mahāyogeśvaraḥ, 'the great lord of yoga', answers Arjuna's own address yogeśvara in v.4. Darśayām āsa is a periphrastic perfect, a formation classical Sanskrit uses for certain derived and causative verbs in place of a simple reduplicated perfect.

weapon (divyānekodyatāyudham: 'having many divine weapons upraised', acc. sg.; divya + aneka → divyāneka, a + a → ā; aneka + udyata → anekodyata, a + u → o; udyata + āyudham → udyatāyudham, a + ā → ā)

sentences.l: Of many mouths and eyes, of many marvelous aspects, of many divine ornaments, with many divine weapons raised —
sentences.i: with countless mouths and eyes, countless wonders to see, countless divine ornaments, and countless divine weapons raised —
sentences.n: This verse and the next are a chain of bahuvrīhi compounds — 'possessive' compounds naming the form by what it has, all in the accusative describing rūpam from v.9 — with no finite verb of their own; the sentence is completed only in v.13's apaśyat, 'he saw'. Each pair of compounds is joined by the same word aneka, 'many, numerous', repeated four times across the two verses, mounting the sense of overwhelming multiplicity.

sentences.t:
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् ।
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
sentences.tr:
divya-mālya-ambara-dharam divya-gandha-anulepanam |
sarva-āścarya-mayam devam anantam viśvataḥ-mukham ||

morph.gloss: divine
garland
garment, robe (mālya + ambara → mālyāmbara, a + a → ā)
wearing, bearing (divyamālyāmbaradharam: 'wearing divine garlands and robes', acc. sg.)
divine
fragrance, perfume
unguent, ointment, anointment (divyagandhānulepanam: 'anointed with divine fragrance', acc. sg.; gandha + anulepanam → gandhānulepanam, a + a → ā)
all
wonder, marvel (sarva + āścarya → sarvāścarya, a + ā → ā)
made of, consisting wholly of (suffix; sarvāścaryamayam: 'all-wondrous', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with devam)
god (acc. sg., the cosmic form of Kṛṣṇa)
endless, infinite (acc. sg.)
from, on every side, in every direction (indeclinable; -as + m- → -o m-)
face, mouth (viśvatomukham: 'having face(s) on every side', acc. sg.)

sentences.l: wearing divine garlands and robes, anointed with divine fragrance — the god all-wondrous, infinite, facing every way.
sentences.i: wearing divine garlands and robes, anointed with heavenly fragrance — a god of every wonder, without end, facing every direction.
sentences.n: The chain of compounds from v.10 concludes here on devam, 'the god' — the grammatical head that all of vv.10–11 have been describing. Viśvatomukham, 'facing every way', is a celebrated old epithet (compare the Vedic viśvataścakṣuḥ, 'eyed on every side'), later echoed at 13.13. Sarvāścaryamayam, 'made wholly of wonder', uses the suffix -maya, '(consisting) of, full of' — the same suffix that will form nāmarūpamaya-type compounds elsewhere in Sanskrit philosophical writing.

sentences.t:
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता ।
यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
sentences.tr:
divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhavet yugapat utthitā |
yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syāt bhāsaḥ tasya mahātmanaḥ ||

morph.gloss: sky, heaven (loc. sg. 'in the sky')
sun
thousand (sūryasahasrasya: 'of a thousand suns', gen. sg.)
to be (bhavet: optative 3rd sg. 'were to be, should arise'; -t + y- → -d y-)
at once, simultaneously (-t + u- → -d u-)
to rise up, arise (utthitā: past participle 'arisen', nom. sg. fem., agreeing with bhāḥ in the next line)
if
light, radiance, splendor (nom. sg. fem.)
similar, like, resembling (nom. sg. fem.)
that, it (sā: nom. sg. fem.)
to be (syāt: optative 3rd sg. 'would be'; -t + bh- → -d bh-)
light, splendor, radiance (bhāsaḥ: gen. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that, he (tasya: gen. sg. 'of that, his')
great-souled, of great spirit (mahā 'great' + ātman 'self'; gen. sg. 'of the great-souled one', i.e. Kṛṣṇa in this cosmic form)

sentences.l: If in the sky the light of a thousand suns should rise up at once, that would be like the splendor of that great-souled one.
sentences.i: If a thousand suns were to blaze up together in the sky, their light would still be no more than a match for the splendor of that great being.
sentences.n: One of the poem's most quoted images. Bhavet and syāt are both optative, 'were to be' / 'would be', framing a contrary-to-fact comparison: 'if X were to happen, Y would be [merely] like it'. Mahātman, 'great-souled', a standard honorific compound (mahā + ātman), here names the being whose splendor exceeds even that thousand-sun light — Kṛṣṇa in his cosmic form. Note the run of sandhi: bhavet + yugapat → bhaved yugapat (-t + y- → -d y-), yugapat + utthitā → yugapad utthitā (-t + u- → -d u-), syāt + bhāsaḥ → syād bhāsaḥ (-t + bh- → -d bh-), bhāsaḥ + tasya → bhāsas tasya (-aḥ + t- → -as t-).

sentences.t:
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा ।
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥
sentences.tr:
tatra eka-stham jagat kṛtsnam pravibhaktam anekadhā |
apaśyat deva-devasya śarīre pāṇḍavaḥ tadā ||

morph.gloss: there
standing in one place, united (eka 'one' + stha 'standing'; acc. sg. neut.; tatra + eka- → tatraika-, a + e → ai)
world, universe (acc. sg. neut.)
whole, entire (acc. sg. neut.)
to divide up, distribute (pravibhakta: past participle 'divided', acc. sg. neut.)
in many ways, manifold (adverb, aneka 'many' + suffix -dhā)
to see (apaśyat: imperfect 3rd sg. 'he saw'; -t + d- → -d d-)
god (devadevasya: 'of the god of gods', gen. sg., Kṛṣṇa in his cosmic form)
body (loc. sg. 'in the body')
son of Pāṇḍu, here Arjuna (nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
then

sentences.l: There, united in one, the whole world divided in many ways, the Pāṇḍava then saw, in the body of the god of gods.
sentences.i: There, in the body of the god of gods, Arjuna then saw the whole universe gathered into one, divided in countless ways.
sentences.n: This verse finally supplies the finite verb, apaśyat, 'he saw', that the long descriptive sentence of vv.9–11 has been waiting for: what Kṛṣṇa showed, Arjuna now sees. Deva-deva, 'the god of gods', is the poem's title for Kṛṣṇa's cosmic form. Eka-stham ... anekadhā, 'united in one ... divided in many ways', sets side by side the paradox at the heart of the vision — the whole universe is at once one thing and countless things.

sentences.t:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनंजयः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
sentences.tr:
tataḥ saḥ vismaya-āviṣṭaḥ hṛṣṭa-romā dhanaṃjayaḥ |
praṇamya śirasā devam kṛtāñjaliḥ abhāṣata ||

morph.gloss: then
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; final -ḥ dropped before a consonant)
astonishment, wonder
to enter (āviṣṭa: past participle 'entered, possessed, overcome', nom. sg. masc.; vismaya + āviṣṭaḥ → vismayāviṣṭaḥ, a + ā → ā; final -aḥ before h- → -o)
bristling, thrilled, standing on end (past participle of hṛṣ)
body-hair (hṛṣṭaromā: nom. sg. masc. bahuvrīhi, 'his hair bristling with awe')
'winner of wealth', Arjuna (nom. sg.; spelled here with anusvāra, dhanaṃjaya, an orthographic variant of dhanañjaya)
to bow down (praṇamya: gerund 'having bowed down')
head (instr. sg. 'with [his] head')
god (acc. sg., the cosmic form of Kṛṣṇa)
to do, make (kṛta: past participle 'made, done')
the cupped-hands gesture of salutation and reverence (kṛtāñjaliḥ: nom. sg. masc. bahuvrīhi, 'with hands folded in añjali'; kṛta + añjaliḥ → kṛtāñjaliḥ, a + a → ā; -iḥ + a- → -ir a-)
to speak (abhāṣata: imperfect middle 3rd sg. 'he spoke')

sentences.l: Then he, overcome with astonishment, his hair bristling, Dhanañjaya — having bowed his head to the god, with hands folded, spoke.
sentences.i: Then Arjuna, overwhelmed with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the god and, hands folded, began to speak.
sentences.n: Vismayāviṣṭaḥ, 'entered by astonishment', uses ā-viś, 'to enter, possess', the same verb that described Arjuna being overcome by pity at 1.28 (kṛpayā parayāviṣṭaḥ); hṛṣṭaromā, 'hair bristling', echoes the shock-symptoms of 1.29 (romaharṣa, 'hair-thrill'), though there from dread and here from awe. Añjali, the cupped-hands gesture of reverence, marks the shift from Sañjaya's narration into the hymn of praise (the Viśvarūpa-stuti) that follows in the verses beyond this chunk. Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth', Arjuna's title, is spelled here with anusvāra for the class nasal — an orthographic variant, not a real one, and needs no correction note.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे ।
सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसंघान् ।
ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ- ।
मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥
sentences.tr:
paśyāmi devān tava deva dehe |
sarvān tathā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃghān |
brahmāṇam īśam kamala-āsana-stha- |
m ṛṣīn ca sarvān uragān ca divyān ||

morph.gloss: to see (paśyāmi: present 1st sg. 'I see')
god (acc. pl. 'the gods'; -n + t- → -ṃs t-)
you (tava: gen. sg. 'your', modifying dehe)
god (vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa: 'O God')
body (loc. sg. 'in [your] body')
all (acc. pl.; -n + t- → -ṃs t-, as in devāṃs above)
likewise, and also
being, creature (first compound member)
particular kind, distinction (second member)
multitude, host (bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃgha: 'hosts of the various kinds of beings', acc. pl.)
Brahmā, the creator-god of the traditional cosmology (a proper name; acc. sg. brahmāṇam; joined directly before the vowel ī- of īśam, no change)
lord, ruler (acc. sg. īśam, in apposition to brahmāṇam: 'Brahmā the lord'; -m before the consonant k- of the next word → anusvāra ṃ)
lotus (first compound member)
seat (second member, kamala-āsana 'lotus-seat')

seated, situated (third member: 'seated on the lotus-seat', describing Brahmā, acc. sg. kamalāsanastham; the Wikisource print line breaks this compound oddly across the pāda break, dropping its final -m — see note)
seated (m: the final -m of kamalāsana-stham, completing the word begun on the previous print line — see note)
sage, seer (ṛṣīn: acc. pl. masc.; -n + c- → -ṃś c-)
and
all (acc. pl.; joined directly before the vowel u- of uragān, no change)
serpent, snake-deity, a Nāga (lit. 'going on the belly'; acc. pl.; -n + c- → -ṃś c-)
and
divine, celestial (acc. pl. masc., agreeing with uragān)

sentences.l: I see the gods, O God, in your body, and likewise all the hosts of the various kinds of beings; Brahmā the lord seated-on-the-lotus-seat, and the sages, and all the divine serpents.
sentences.i: In your body I see the gods, O God, and with them the hosts of every kind of being; Brahmā the creator seated on his lotus, the sages, and all the divine serpents.
sentences.n: This is the chapter's first triṣṭubh (four-line, eleven-syllable) verse; from here through the rest of Arjuna's speech the grander triṣṭubh replaces the śloka couplets used earlier in the chapter. The Wikisource print breaks the compound kamalāsana-stham, 'seated on the lotus-seat' (describing Brahmā), oddly across the pāda boundary: कमलासनस्थ- ends line 3 and the bare म् completing it opens line 4 before ऋषींश्च; the two are drafted as separate words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of chapter 9 verse 20's सुरेन्द्रलोक-/मश्नन्ति split. Brahmā, born on a lotus from Viṣṇu's navel in the epic cosmology, is named here alongside the sages and the divine serpents (nāgas) as inhabitants of the cosmic form, signalling that the whole created order is visible within it.

sentences.t:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं ।
पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् ।
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं ।
पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥
sentences.tr:
aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram |
paśyāmi tvām sarvataḥ ananta-rūpam |
na antam na madhyam na punaḥ tava ādim |

arm (second member; -u + u- → -ū- with udara, undone at the hyphen)
belly (third member)
mouth, face (fourth member)
eye (aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netra: 'having many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes', bahuvrīhi, acc. sg. masc. -netram, describing tvām; -m before the consonant p- of paśyāmi → anusvāra ṃ)
to see (paśyāmi: present 1st sg.)
you (acc. sg. tvām, the vulgate's anusvāra spelling; BORI reads tvā, the enclitic accusative, instead — see note)
from all sides, everywhere (adverb; -as + a- → -o, with the avagraha marking the lost a-)
endless, infinite (first compound member)
form (ananta-rūpa: 'of infinite form', acc. sg., agreeing with tvām)
not (na + a- → nā-)
end (acc. sg. neut.; -m before the consonant n- of the next word → anusvāra ṃ)
not

not

you (tava: gen. sg. 'your')
beginning (ādim: acc. sg.; -a + ā- → -ā-; -m before the vowel-initial paśyāmi of the next line is retained as written -m — see note)
to see (paśyāmi: present 1st sg.)
universe, all (first compound member)
lord, ruler (viśva-īśvara: 'Lord of the universe', vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa; -a + ī- → -e-)
universe, all (first compound member)
form (viśva-rūpa: 'having the universe as your form, universal-formed', vocative sg., addressed to Kṛṣṇa — the epithet that gives this chapter its name)

sentences.l: Many-armed-bellied-mouthed-eyed, I see you, on-every-side of-infinite-form; no end, no middle, nor again your beginning do I see, O Lord-of-the-universe, universal-formed one.
sentences.i: I see you with countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, your form without end on every side; I find no end, no middle, and no beginning in you, Lord of the universe, you whose very form is the universe.
sentences.n: BORI reads tvā (the enclitic accusative) for the vulgate's tvāṃ. The compound anekabāhūdaravaktranetram, 'having many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes', undoes at the hyphen the vowel fusion bāhu + udara → bāhūdara. Viśveśvara ('Lord of the universe') and viśvarūpa ('having the universe as your form') are the two vocatives that name this chapter's vision; the second gives the chapter its title, Viśvarūpadarśana.

sentences.t:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च ।
तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् ।
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता- ।
द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥
sentences.tr:
kirīṭinam gadinam cakriṇam ca |
tejo-rāśim sarvataḥ dīptimantam |
paśyāmi tvām durnirīkṣyam samantā- |
d dīpta-anala-arka-dyutim aprameyam ||

morph.gloss: crowned, wearing a diadem (from kirīṭa 'crown, diadem' + the possessive suffix -in; acc. sg. masc., describing tvām; -m before the consonant g- → anusvāra ṃ)
bearing a mace (from gadā 'mace, club' + -in; acc. sg. masc.; -m before c- → anusvāra ṃ)

bearing a discus (from cakra 'discus, wheel' + -in; acc. sg. masc.; -m before the vowel-initial ca is retained as written -m, but before a following consonant would nasalize — here followed by च, a consonant, so -m before c- → anusvāra ṃ)
and
brilliance, splendor, fiery energy (first compound member; -as + r- → -o r-)
heap, mass (tejo-rāśi: 'a mass of radiance', acc. sg., describing tvām)

blazing, radiant, possessing splendor (acc. sg. masc., describing tvām)
to see (paśyāmi: present 1st sg.)
you (acc. sg.)

on all sides (d: the final -t of samantāt, voiced to -d by sandhi before the following d-, completing the word begun on the previous print line — see note)
to blaze, shine (dīpta: past participle 'blazing', first member of the following compound; -a + a- → -ā- with anala, undone at the hyphen)
fire (second member; -a + a- → -ā- with arka, undone at the hyphen)
sun (third member)
light, radiance (dīpta-anala-arka-dyuti: 'the blazing light of fire and sun', fourth member, describing tvām, acc. sg. -dyutim)
immeasurable, unfathomable (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with tvām)

sentences.l: Crowned, mace-bearing, discus-bearing, a mass-of-radiance blazing on every side, I see you, hard-to-behold, on-all-sides blazing-with-the-light-of-fire-and-sun, immeasurable.
sentences.i: I see you crowned, bearing mace and discus, a mass of light blazing on every side, hard to look at, ablaze all around like fire and sun, beyond all measure.
sentences.n: The Wikisource print breaks the phrase samantāt dīptānalārkadyutim, '[blazing] on all sides with the light of fire and sun', across the pāda boundary: समन्ता- ends line 3, dropping the word's final -t; that -t resurfaces, voiced to -d by sandhi before the following d-, as the bare द् that opens line 4's द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम्. Drafted as two words-entries to tile the source exactly, on the model of chapter 9 verse 20's सुरेन्द्रलोक-/मश्नन्ति split (cf. verse 15 above). Kirīṭin, gadin, cakrin are all -in possessive formations, 'crown-having', 'mace-having', 'discus-having' — three of Viṣṇu's traditional emblems (the fourth, the lotus, is not named here).

sentences.t:
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं ।
त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता ।
सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥
sentences.tr:
tvam akṣaram paramam veditavyam |
tvam asya viśvasya param nidhānam |
tvam avyayaḥ śāśvata-dharma-goptā |
sanātanaḥ tvam puruṣaḥ mataḥ me ||

morph.gloss: you (nom. sg., predicate subject of an implied 'are'; joined directly before the vowel a- of akṣaram, no change)
the Imperishable, the indestructible (nom. sg. neut., used as a name for the changeless absolute; -m before the consonant p- → anusvāra ṃ)
supreme (nom. sg. neut.; -m before v- → anusvāra ṃ)
to know (veditavya: gerundive 'to be known', nom. sg. neut.: 'the object of knowledge')
you (nom. sg.; joined directly before the vowel a- of asya, no change)
this (asya: gen. sg. neut. 'of this', referring to viśvasya)
universe, all (gen. sg. 'of the universe')
supreme, highest (here param: nom. sg. neut.; -m before n- → anusvāra ṃ)
receptacle, resting-place, treasure-house (nom. sg. neut.)
you (nom. sg.; joined directly before the vowel a- of avyayaḥ, no change)
imperishable, undiminishing (nom. sg. masc.)
eternal, everlasting (first compound member)
the sacred order, the cosmic law (second member, kept untranslated in idiomatic sense per house style)
to guard, protect (goptṛ: agent noun 'guardian', third member, nom. sg.: 'the guardian of eternal dharma')
eternal, ancient, everlasting (nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
you (nom. sg.; -m before the consonant p- → anusvāra ṃ)
the Person, the cosmic Spirit (a central Sāṃkhya and Upaniṣadic term for the ultimate self; nom. sg.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
to think (mata: past participle 'thought, deemed, considered', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)

sentences.l: You are the Imperishable, the supreme thing-to-be-known; you are of this universe the supreme resting-place; you are imperishable, the guardian of eternal-dharma; the eternal one, you, the Person, are thought by me.
sentences.i: You are the Imperishable, the highest object of knowledge. You are the ultimate resting-place of this whole universe. You are the undying guardian of eternal dharma. You are, I believe, the eternal, primeval Person.
sentences.n: Four parallel tvam-clauses (tvam akṣaram, tvam asya ... parama nidhānam, tvam avyayaḥ, sanātanas tvam) name Kṛṣṇa with a string of philosophical titles: akṣara, 'the Imperishable', is a standard Upaniṣadic name for the changeless absolute; puruṣa, 'the Person', is the term Sāṃkhya uses for the ultimate self, here identified with Kṛṣṇa outright. Dharma in śāśvata-dharma-goptā is the cosmic order in the general sense (left untranslated per house style), not any one family's custom, as elsewhere in the poem. Mato me, 'thought by me', is a past participle with its agent in the instrumental — the ordinary Sanskrit way of saying 'I think, in my view'.

sentences.t:
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य- ।

पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं ।
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥
sentences.tr:
an-ādi-madhya-antam ananta-vīrya- |
m ananta-bāhum śaśi-sūrya-netram |

sentences.i: I see you without beginning, middle, or end, your power boundless, your arms without number, the sun and moon your eyes; your mouth ablaze like fire, scorching this whole universe with your own radiance.
sentences.n: The Wikisource print breaks anantavīryam, 'of infinite power', across the pāda boundary, printing अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य- at the end of line 1 and completing it with a bare म् at the start of line 2 before अनन्तबाहुं; here the leftover म् simply attaches to the following vowel-initial word with no further sandhi change. Drafted as two words-entries to tile the source exactly, on the model of chapter 9 verse 20's सुरेन्द्रलोक-/मश्नन्ति split (cf. verses 15 and 17 above). An-ādi-madhya-anta is a four-member bahuvrīhi, 'having no beginning, middle, or end'; hutāśa, literally 'oblation-eater', is an old epithet of Agni, fire, used here as a plain word for fire itself.

व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः ।
दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं ।
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥

sentences.l: This the-space-between-heaven-and-earth indeed is pervaded by-you-alone, and the-directions, all of them; having-seen this wonderful, terrible form of-yours, the-triple-world trembles, O great-souled one.
sentences.i: This space between heaven and earth, and all the directions besides, are filled by you alone. Having seen this astonishing, terrible form of yours, the three worlds tremble, great soul.
sentences.n: BORI reads rūpam idaṃ tavograṃ (transposing idam and ugram/tava) for the vulgate's rūpam ugraṃ tavedaṃ; the sense is unchanged. Dyāvāpṛthivī, 'heaven-and-earth', is a fixed Vedic dvandva compound, always dual; its whole space (antaram) is said to be filled by Kṛṣṇa's form alone. Mahātman, 'great-souled', addresses Kṛṣṇa directly for the first time in this vision, a title the poem elsewhere also gives to sages and heroes.

sentences.t:

केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति ।
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसंघाः ।
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥

sentences.l: These hosts-of-gods indeed enter you; some, frightened, hands-folded, cry-out; having-said 'Hail!', the-hosts-of-great-sages-and-perfected-beings praise you with-abundant hymns-of-praise.
sentences.i: These hosts of gods enter into you; some, terrified, cry out with hands folded in reverence; the hosts of great sages and perfected beings, crying 'Hail!', praise you with abundant hymns.
sentences.n: BORI reads tvā (the enclitic accusative) for the vulgate's tvāṃ. Amī, 'those, these', is the nominative plural of the distal demonstrative adas, referring here to the gods now visible entering Kṛṣṇa's gaping mouths, an image the chapter develops further in the verses that follow this excerpt. Svastīty uktvā, 'having said svasti', is the standard Vedic blessing-cry, 'hail! all is well!', cried out by the sages and perfected beings at the terrifying sight.

गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसंघा ।
वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥

sentences.l: The-Rudras-and-Ādityas, the Vasus, and whichever Sādhyas there are; the-Viśvedevas, the-two-Aśvins, the Maruts and the-steam-drinking-ancestors, and the-hosts-of-gandharvas-yakṣas-asuras-and-siddhas — they gaze-at you, astonished, all indeed.
sentences.i: The Rudras and Ādityas, the Vasus, and whatever Sādhyas there are; the Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the ancestral spirits who feed on the sacrificial steam; the hosts of gandharvas, yakṣas, asuras, and siddhas — all of them stare at you, astonished.
sentences.n: BORI reads tvā (the enclitic accusative) for the vulgate's tvāṃ, in vīkṣante tvāṃ. The verse rolls out the classes of Vedic gods: the eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, eight Vasus, the Sādhyas and Viśvedevas (minor divine classes), the twin horsemen Aśvins, the storm-gods Maruts, and the uṣmapāḥ, 'steam-drinkers' — an epithet of the Pitṛs, the ancestral spirits, who partake of the rising heat of the offerings. Alongside them stand gandharvas (celestial musicians), yakṣas (nature-spirits), asuras (demons) and siddhas (perfected beings): every order of being in the traditional cosmos, all astonished at once.

sentences.t:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं ।

sentences.l: Your great form, many-mouthed-and-eyed, O mighty-armed one, many-armed-thighed-and-footed, many-bellied, terrible-with-many-fangs — having seen it, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
sentences.i: Seeing your vast form, mighty-armed one, with its many mouths and eyes, its many arms, thighs, and feet, its many bellies and its rows of terrible fangs, the worlds tremble — and so do I.
sentences.n: Mahābāho, 'mighty-armed', addresses Kṛṣṇa even as Arjuna describes the terror of what he sees — an epithet more often given to warriors, turned here onto the god in his monstrous form. Bahu-bāhu-ūru-pādam undoes the vowel fusion bāhu + ūru → bāhūru at the hyphen, and bahūdaram undoes bahu + udara → bahūdara the same way. Tathāham, 'and so I too', ends the verse: even Arjuna, who asked to see this form, is now as shaken as the onlooking worlds.

sentences.i: Touching the sky, blazing, many-colored, your mouth wide open, your eyes huge and blazing — having seen you, my innermost self trembles; I can find no steadiness, no peace, Viṣṇu.
sentences.n: Viṣṇu, kept untranslated as the proper name it is, appears here for the first time in this vision as a name addressed to Kṛṣṇa, identifying him outright with the great preserver-god of the classical triad. Nabhaḥ-spṛśam, 'touching the sky', keeps its visarga unchanged before the following voiceless s-. The compound pravyathita-antar-ātmā, 'whose inmost self is trembling', names Arjuna's own state, not Kṛṣṇa's: the subject shifts here from the 'you' of the first two lines to the 'I' who is speaking.

sentences.l: Fang-terrible your mouths, having-seen indeed, resembling-the-fire-of-doomsday — the directions I know not, nor do I find peace; be gracious, O lord-of-gods, abode-of-the-universe.
sentences.i: Seeing your mouths, terrible with fangs, like the fires that end the world, I lose all sense of direction and find no peace. Have mercy, lord of the gods, abode of the universe!
sentences.n: Daṃṣṭrā-karālāni ('terrible with fangs') and kāla-analasannibhāni ('resembling the fire of doomsday') both describe mukhāni, the object of dṛṣṭvā; kālānala, 'the fire of Time', is the conflagration that ends each cosmic age — the same kāla that names itself outright in verse 32. Arjuna's speech, begun at v.15, continues uninterrupted through v.31. Deveśa and jagannivāsa are two vocatives addressed to the cosmic form: 'lord of the gods' and 'abode of the universe' (jagat + nivāsa, -t + n- → -n n-).

sentences.l: And these, you — the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all of them, together indeed with hosts-of-kings; Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and the charioteer's-son likewise, he too, together with our own chief-warriors too —
sentences.i: And these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all of them, together with hosts of kings, rush toward you — Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Karṇa the charioteer's son too, together with our own chief warriors —
sentences.n: Verses 26–27 are a single sentence: the subject amī ... putrāḥ ... sarve, 'these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all of them', with the list of named warriors here, and the verb viśanti, 'they enter', arriving only in v.27. Tvām, accusative, anticipates that verb and is resumed there by vaktrāṇi te, 'your mouths' — 'they enter you, [namely] your mouths'. Sūtaputra, 'the charioteer's son', names Karṇa without naming him, the epic's usual discretion about his birth.

sentences.n: Completes the sentence begun in v.26: subject amī ... putrāḥ ... sarve, verb viśanti, object vaktrāṇi te. Daṃṣṭrā-karālāni repeats the phrase from v.25, now describing the mouths directly instead of through a gerund. Uttamāṅga, 'the highest limb', is a standard periphrasis for 'the head'.

sentences.n: A hyphen split across the pāda boundary: the sandhi lokāḥ + tava → lokās tava is printed split by Wikisource as लोका- at the end of the third line and स्तवापि at the start of the fourth; the leftover स् that opens स्तवापि completes लोकाः, drafted here as two words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of ch09 v.20's सुरेन्द्रलोक-/मश्नन्ति split. Samṛddhavegāḥ, 'with gathered speed', is used twice, first of the moths, then of the doomed people, tying the simile tightly to its object.

sentences.l: Tell me who you are, of fierce-form; homage be to you, O best-of-gods, be gracious. I wish to know fully you, the primal one; for I do not understand your course-of-action.
sentences.i: Tell me who you are, in this terrible form. Homage to you, best of gods — have mercy! I want to understand you, the primal being; I cannot fathom what you are doing.
sentences.n: Closes Arjuna's speech (begun at v.15) with a direct question, answered at once in v.32. Pravṛtti, 'activity, course, function', is broad — what the form is doing, and to what end.

sentences.l: Time I am, world-destruction-making, grown-great, here set-in-motion to gather in the worlds; even without you, all these warriors standing in the opposing ranks will not be.
sentences.i: I am Time, grown vast, the wrecker of worlds, at work here to gather the worlds in. Even without you, none of the warriors drawn up in the facing lines will survive.
sentences.n: The pivot of the chapter: kāla is Time itself — the impersonal power that both generates and dissolves the worlds — not 'Death', the famous rendering this drafting does not follow. Pravṛddhaḥ ('grown vast') and pravṛttaḥ ('now at work'), both nominative in apposition to kālaḥ, present Time as already immense and already in motion; lokān samāhartum, 'to gather in the worlds', casts the destruction as a harvest rather than a slaughter. Ṛte governs the accusative tvām, 'apart from you', the same construction found elsewhere in this chapter (vv.16, 20–22). BORI reads tvā (enclitic accusative) for the vulgate's tvāṃ.

sentences.l: Therefore, you, arise, win fame; having conquered your enemies, enjoy a flourishing kingdom. By me indeed already these have been slain, beforehand; be a mere instrument, O ambidextrous archer.

sentences.n: Nimitta-mātram, 'a mere occasion, a mere instrument', is the verse's famous phrase: Arjuna is not the true agent of the killing, already accomplished by kāla, but only its visible means. Savyasācin, 'able to shoot with the left hand too', names Arjuna's ambidexterity as a warrior.

sentences.l: Droṇa and Bhīṣma and Jayadratha and Karṇa, and likewise other warrior-heroes too — slain already by me, you, kill! Do not waver; fight — a conqueror you are, in battle, over your rivals.
sentences.i: Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa, and the other warrior-heroes too — they are already slain by me; you need only strike them down. Do not waver — fight! You will be victorious over your rivals in battle.
sentences.n: Continues v.33's teaching with a list of the very men Arjuna most dreads killing, all declared already slain. Jetāsi, 'you are a conqueror', a present-tense statement of a settled future, echoes kāla's claim in v.32 that the outcome is already fixed. Mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ, 'do not waver', is a prohibitive with the aorist injunctive, the mood regularly used with mā.

the gesture of cupped, folded hands raised in reverence (kṛta-añjali: 'one who has made the añjali', i.e. 'with hands folded in homage', nom. sg. masc.; -iḥ + v- → -ir v-)

crowned, wearing a diadem; an epithet of Arjuna, from the diadem given him by Indra (nom. sg. masc.)

sentences.l: This word of the slayer-of-Keśin having-heard, with-folded-hands, trembling, the-crowned-one, having-done-homage, again indeed spoke to Kṛṣṇa — brokenly, frightened-again-and-again, having-prostrated.
sentences.i: Hearing this from Keśava, Arjuna, the crowned one, folded his hands and, trembling, bowed low; then, his voice breaking, utterly afraid, he prostrated himself and spoke again to Kṛṣṇa.
sentences.n: The whole verse is one sentence, still narrated by Sañjaya: a chain of participles and gerunds (kṛtāñjaliḥ 'with folded hands', vepamānaḥ 'trembling', namaskṛtvā 'having bowed', bhīta-bhītaḥ 'utterly afraid', praṇamya 'having prostrated') built around the single finite verb āha, 'he spoke'. Kirīṭī, 'the crowned one' — from the diadem Indra gave him — and Keśava, 'having fine hair' or 'slayer of the demon Keśin', are epithets of Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa respectively. Sandhi: एतच्छ्रुत्वा is etat + śrutvā (-t + ś- → -c ch-); कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः is kṛtāñjaliḥ + vepamānaḥ (-iḥ + v- → -ir v-); भूय एवाह shows bhūyaḥ losing its visarga entirely before the vowel e- of eva — before a non-a vowel a final -aḥ simply drops, with no -o and no avagraha, unlike before a- — and then eva + āha: a + ā → ā.

स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या ।
जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च ।

सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसंघाः ॥

sarve namasyanti ca siddha-saṃghāḥ ||

sentences.l: Fitting it is, O lord-of-the-senses, at-your renown, the-world rejoices and-becomes-delighted; the-demons, frightened, to-the-directions flee; all indeed pay-homage, and the-hosts-of-siddhas.
sentences.i: It is fitting, Hṛṣīkeśa, that at your renown the world rejoices and is filled with delight; the demons, terrified, flee in every direction; and all the hosts of the perfected ones bow down.
sentences.n: Sthāne is an adverbial idiom, 'fittingly, it stands to reason', not a literal 'in the place'; this opens Arjuna's hymn of praise (stuti) that runs through the rest of the chapter. Rakṣāṃsi, 'rākṣasas, demons', flee in terror while the siddhas, 'perfected, accomplished beings' (a class of minor divinities), bow down — the universal awe Sañjaya has just narrated from the outside is now Arjuna's own theme. Sandhi: जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते packs jagat + prahṛṣyati (simply written joined, no phonetic change) + prahṛṣyati + anurajyate (-i + a- → -y a-); दिशो is diśaḥ, -aḥ before d- → -o.

अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास ।

sentences.l: And-why should-they not bow to-you, O great-souled-one, greater even-than Brahmā, the-original-creator; O endless-one, O lord-of-gods, O abode-of-the-universe — you are the-imperishable, being-and-non-being, and what is beyond-that.
sentences.i: And why should they not bow to you, great one — you who are greater even than Brahmā, the first creator? Endless one, lord of the gods, dwelling-place of the universe: you are the imperishable — being and non-being, and what lies beyond both.
sentences.n: ब्रह्मणः here names the god Brahmā, the creator (an ablative of comparison with garīyase, 'greater than Brahmā'): a proper name, not the abstract, untranslated brahman of the conventions. The context — 'greater even than Brahmā, the original creator [ādikartre]' — makes plain this is the personal creator-god, one figure among those Kṛṣṇa is said to surpass, not the impersonal absolute; it is capitalized and translated as a name accordingly. Akṣaram, sad-asat, tat param, and the closing yat build the same formula found at 13.12 and echoed elsewhere in the poem: the imperishable is what is 'being and non-being, and what is beyond both'. Sandhi: कस्माच्च is kasmāt + ca (-t + c- → -c c-); नमेरन्महात्मन् simply writes nameran + mahātman joined, with no phonetic change, as consonant-final words are often printed in this text; ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे packs brahmaṇaḥ + api (-aḥ + a- → -o ' with avagraha) + api + ādikartre (-i + ā- → -y ā-); जगन्निवास is jagat + nivāsa (-t + n- → -n n-); सदसत्तत्परं packs sat + asat (-t + a- → -d a-) + asat + tat (-t + t- → -t t-, written doubled).

त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥

sentences.l: You are the-primal-god, the-Person, the-ancient-one; you are of-this universe the-supreme resting-place. You are the-knower and the-knowable, and the-supreme abode; by-you is pervaded the-universe, O-one-of-infinite-form.
sentences.i: You are the primal god, the ancient Person; you are the supreme resting-place of this universe. You are the knower and the known, and the highest abode; by you this whole universe is pervaded, boundless in form.
sentences.n: The Wikisource print line breaks the word पुराणस्त्वम् (purāṇaḥ + tvam, 'you are ancient') exactly at the pāda boundary, into पुराण- and स्त्वमस्य; the two are one continuous phrase — purāṇaḥ (nom. sg., predicate) + tvam asya ('you, of this [universe]') — with the visarga of purāṇaḥ turning to -s- before the following t-, and are drafted here as two words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of chapter 9 verse 20's sura-indra-lokam/aśnanti split. Puruṣa, the cosmic Person or Spirit set against prakṛti ('nature') in the Sāṃkhya scheme, is translated here as 'the Person' rather than left untranslated, since it is not among the terms the conventions single out (dharma, yoga, brahman, the guṇas, sāṃkhya). Vettā...vedyam plays on the root vid, 'to know': Kṛṣṇa is named both the knower and the known. Sandhi: वेत्तासि is vettā + asi (ā + a → ā).

sentences.t:
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः ।
प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च ।
नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः ।
पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥

sentences.l: Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the-moon; Prajāpati are you, and the-great-grandfather too. Homage, homage to-you be — a-thousand-times; and-again and yet-again, homage, homage to-you!
sentences.i: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon; you are Prajāpati, and the great-grandfather beyond him. Homage to you, homage, a thousand times over — and again, and yet again, homage, homage to you!
sentences.n: A catalogue verse identifying Kṛṣṇa with the great gods of the Vedic pantheon — Vāyu (wind), Yama (death), Agni (fire), Varuṇa (the waters), the moon, Prajāpati ('lord of creatures', a creator-deity) — and then with prapitāmaha, 'the great-grandfather', one step beyond even Brahmā, the grandfather-creator named in the previous verse. The second half is a chant of repeated prostration, namo namas te...namo namas te, 'homage, homage to you', doubled for intensity and repeated a second time. Sandhi: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः packs vāyuḥ + yamaḥ (-uḥ + y- → -ur y-) + yamaḥ + agniḥ (-aḥ + a- → -o ' with avagraha) + agniḥ + varuṇaḥ (-iḥ + v- → -ir v-); प्रजापतिस्त्वं is prajāpatiḥ + tvam (-iḥ + t- → -is t-, visarga before a voiceless consonant); नमस्तेऽस्तु packs namaḥ + te (-aḥ + t- → -as t-) + te + astu (-e + a- → -e ' with avagraha, as at ch01 33's ta ime 'vasthitāḥ); सर्वत (verse 40) drops its visarga entirely before eva, the same non-a-vowel rule as verse 35's bhūya eva.

sentences.i: Homage to you from in front, and homage from behind; homage to you from every side, O you who are all! You are of boundless might and measureless prowess; you pervade everything, and so you are everything.
sentences.n: The prostration of verse 39 continues from every direction — front, back, every side — and the verse closes on a wordplay: sarva, 'all', names Kṛṣṇa as the universal being who samāpnoṣi, 'pervades, fully comprehends', sarvam, 'everything', and so tataḥ, 'therefore', asi sarvaḥ, 'you are all'. Sandhi: पुरस्तादथ is purastāt + atha (-t + a- → -d a-); पृष्ठतस्ते is pṛṣṭhataḥ + te (-aḥ + t- → -as t-); नमोऽस्तु and ततोऽसि both show -aḥ + a- → -o ' with avagraha; अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं packs vīrya + amita (a + a → ā) and the compound's own visarga + tvam (-aḥ + t- → -as t-).

sentences.l: Thinking [you] 'a friend', whatever presumptuously was said — 'Hey Kṛṣṇa, hey Yādava, hey friend!' — by me, not knowing this greatness of yours, out of carelessness or out of affection —
sentences.i: Thinking of you only as a friend, and not knowing this greatness of yours, whatever I carelessly said — or said out of affection — 'Hey Kṛṣṇa! Hey Yādava! Hey friend!' —
sentences.n: Verses 41–44 are one long sentence, built on a relative-correlative pair spread across four verses: yad uktam here in the first line ('whatever was said') and yac cāvahāsārtham asatkṛto 'si in 42.1 ('and whatever disrespect you suffered in jest') are both picked up by the two instances of tat in 42.4 (tatsamakṣam, tatkṣāmaye, 'in [your/their] presence... for that I ask forgiveness'). This verse itself has no finite verb; it is the first half of that suspended clause, continued in 42. Note sakheti twice: sakhā + iti, 'thinking "a friend"' and, closing the quoted greeting, '"...a friend!"' — the same fusion, -ā + i- → -e-, seen throughout the chapter (cf. 1.1 pāṇḍavāś caiva). Ajānatā (line 3) and mayā (line 4) are separated by the line break but form one phrase, 'by me, not knowing'; Sanskrit lets an adjective and the noun it modifies fall on either side of an intervening word or line. Yādava, 'descendant of Yadu', is another name for Kṛṣṇa, born into the Yadu clan.

sentences.t:
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि ।
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु ।
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं ।
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yat ca avahāsa-artham asatkṛtaḥ asi |
vihāra-śayyā-āsana-bhojaneṣu |
ekaḥ athavā api acyuta tat samakṣam |
tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam ||

morph.gloss: which, what (relative pronoun, picking up alongside yad uktam of the previous verse; -t + c- → -c c-, written yacca)
and
mockery, joking, ridicule (avahāsa-artham: 'for the sake of a joke', first compound member; -a + a- → -ā-, written joined)
purpose, sake (avahāsārtham: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially, second compound member; written joined with the following word, -m + a- unchanged)
treated improperly, disrespected (asatkṛtaḥ: past participle, nom. sg. masc., 'you were treated with disrespect'; -aḥ + a- → -o-, the following a- elided, marked by avagraha)
to be (asi: present 2nd sg. 'you are')
sport, recreation, play (first compound member)
bed, lying down, resting (second compound member)
seat, sitting (third compound member; śayyā + āsana → -ā + ā- → -ā-, written joined)
eating, a meal (compound bhojaneṣu: loc. pl., 'in play, in resting, in sitting, or in eating')
one, alone (nom. sg. masc., 'alone', describing the circumstance — whether private or in company)
or else, or (disjunctive particle; -aḥ + a- → -o-, elided a marked by avagraha)
even, also (emphatic particle; athavā + api → -ā + a- → -ā-)
'the Unfallen', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (vocative sg.; api + a- → apy a-, the i of api becomes y before the following vowel)
that (acc. sg. neut., resuming yad uktam and yac...asi)
in [one's] presence, openly, before the eyes (adverbial acc.; written joined with tat, -t + s- unchanged)
that (acc. sg. neut., object of kṣāmaye, resuming all that was said above)
to forgive, be patient (kṣāmaye: causative present 1st sg. middle, 'I beg pardon for, I ask to be forgiven')
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of kṣāmaye)
I (aham: nom. sg. subject; tvām + aham written joined, -m + a- unchanged)
immeasurable, unfathomable (aprameyam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with tvām, 'you the immeasurable')

sentences.l: And whatever, for the sake of a joke, you were treated disrespectfully — in play, in bed, at the seat, or at meals, — whether alone, O Unshakeable one, or also in [their] presence — for that I ask you, the immeasurable one, to forgive [me].
sentences.i: and for whatever disrespect I showed you in jest — at play, in bed, at table, sitting together — whether we were alone, Acyuta, or in company, I ask you, the immeasurable one, to forgive it all.
sentences.n: The correlative begun in 41 (yad uktam...) resolves here: tatsamakṣam and tatkṣāmaye both use tat, but to different ends — the first is an adverbial compound, tat-samakṣam, 'in that [company's] presence, openly' (paired with ekaḥ, 'alone', to mean 'whether privately or in front of others'), the second is the plain accusative object of kṣāmaye, 'I ask pardon for that [whole list of offenses]'. Two long lines are single unbroken tokens on Wikisource because they carry no internal word-breaking sandhi that would otherwise split them onto separate print words: yac cāvahāsārthamasatkṛto 'si strings together yat, ca, avahāsārtham ('for the sake of a joke') and asatkṛto 'si ('you were treated improperly'); vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu lists, in one locative plural compound, the settings — play, rest, sitting, meals. Acyuta, 'the Unfallen', is an epithet of Kṛṣṇa. Kṣāmaye is a causative from kṣam 'to forgive, be patient' used in the sense 'I beg to be forgiven, I crave pardon'.

sentences.t:
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य ।
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् ।
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो ।
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥
sentences.tr:
pitā asi lokasya cara-acarasya |
tvam asya pūjyaḥ ca guruḥ garīyān |
na tvat-samaḥ asti abhyadhikaḥ kutaḥ anyaḥ |
loka-traye api a-pratima-prabhāva ||

morph.gloss: father (pitā: nom. sg., 'you are the father'; pitā + asi → -ā + a- → -ā-, elided)
to be (asi: present 2nd sg. 'you are')
world (gen. sg. 'of the world')
moving, animate (first compound member)
unmoving, inanimate (cara-acarasya: gen. sg., 'of the moving and the unmoving'; -a + a- → -ā-, written caracarasya)
you (tvam: nom. sg.)
this (asya: gen. sg. neut., 'of this [world]', referring back to loka; tvam + asya written joined, -m + a- unchanged)
to honor, revere (pūjya: gerundive, nom. sg. masc., 'worthy of honor, to be revered'; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
teacher, one to be revered (nom. sg.; -aḥ + g- → -ar g-)
weightier, more venerable, greater (comparative of guru; nom. sg. masc.)
not
you (tvat: abl. sg. used in a compound, 'than you')
equal (tvat-sama: 'equal to you', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ + a- → -o-, elided a marked by avagraha)
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg. 'there is'; tvatsamaḥ + asti → tvatsamo'sti, as above)
surpassing, superior (abhyadhikaḥ: nom. sg. masc.; asti + abhyadhikaḥ → -i + a- → -y a-, written asty abhyadhikaḥ)
whence, how (interrogative adverb)

other, another (anyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., 'another [one]'; kutaḥ + anyaḥ → -aḥ + a- → -o-, elided a marked by avagraha; the resulting anyaḥ then shows -aḥ → -o before the voiced l- of lokatraye in the next line, a visarga sandhi carried across the pāda break)
world (first compound member)
triad, three (loka-traya: 'the three worlds', loc. sg. loka-traye, 'in the three worlds')
even, also (emphatic particle; -e + a- → -e-, elided a marked by avagraha)
unequalled, without compare (first member of the vocative compound; api + a- → apy a-, glide as above)
power, might, majesty (a-pratima-prabhāva: 'whose majesty is unequalled', vocative sg. masc., addressing Kṛṣṇa)

sentences.l: You are the father of the world, of the moving and the unmoving; you are its one-to-be-honored and its more-venerable teacher; there is not one equal to you — how then another surpassing [you] — even in the three worlds, O one of unequalled majesty.
sentences.i: You are the father of this whole world, of everything that moves and everything that does not; you are its object of reverence and its teacher, greater than any. No one equals you — let alone surpasses you — in all three worlds, you whose majesty has no parallel.
sentences.n: Cara-acara, 'moving and unmoving', is the standard Sanskrit merism for 'everything that lives and everything that does not' — the whole created world. The verse builds a small climax: na tvatsamaḥ, 'not your equal'; kuto 'nyo 'bhyadhikaḥ, 'how [could there be] another surpassing [you]' — 'not even your equal, let alone your better'. Loka-traya, 'the triple world', is the traditional three: heaven, earth, and the netherworld (or, in some readings, heaven, earth, and the middle atmosphere). Guru, 'teacher', takes its own comparative form garīyān, 'weightier, more venerable' — an ordinary Sanskrit pattern, an adjective compared by a separate comparative stem rather than a suffix on itself.

sentences.t:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं ।
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् ।
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः ।
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyam |
prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam |
pitā iva putrasya sakhā iva sakhyuḥ |
priyaḥ priyāyāḥ arhasi deva soḍhum ||

morph.gloss: therefore, for that reason (ablative used adverbially)
to bow down, prostrate oneself (praṇamya: gerund, 'having bowed down'; written joined with tasmāt, -t + p- unchanged)
to place down, fix, prostrate (praṇidhāya: gerund, 'having bowed, having prostrated')
body (acc. sg., object of praṇamya/praṇidhāya)
to become calm, gracious (prasādaye: causative present 1st sg. middle, 'I seek to propitiate, I beg the favor of')
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of prasādaye)
I (aham: nom. sg. subject; tvām + aham written joined, -m + a- unchanged)
lord, ruler (īśam: acc. sg., in apposition to tvām, 'you the lord'; aham + īśam written joined, -m + ī- unchanged)
praiseworthy, worthy of adoration (gerundive of īḍ 'to praise'; īḍyam: acc. sg., in apposition to tvām; īśam + īḍyam written joined, -m + ī- unchanged)
father (pitā: nom. sg.; pitā + iva → -ā + i- → -e-)
like, as (comparative particle)
son (gen. sg., 'of a son')
friend (sakhā: nom. sg.; sakhā + iva → -ā + i- → -e-, cf. pitā + iva above)
like, as (comparative particle)
friend (sakhyuḥ: gen. sg., 'of a friend')
dear, beloved (priyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., 'the loving one', subject of arhasi)
the beloved, a dear one (f.) (priyāyāḥ: gen. sg. fem., 'of the beloved', continuing the series pitā...putrasya, sakhā...sakhyuḥ)
to deserve, ought, be worthy (arhasi: present 2nd sg. 'you ought, you should'; priyāyāḥ + arhasi → -āḥ + a- → -ā-, the visarga drops before the vowel since the preceding vowel is long ā)
god, O God (vocative sg.)
to bear, endure, put up with (soḍhum: infinitive, 'to bear, to endure', complement of arhasi)

sentences.l: Therefore, having bowed, having prostrated [my] body, I seek to win your favor, [you] the lord, worthy of praise; as a father [bears] with a son, as a friend with a friend, as a lover with the beloved, you ought, O God, to bear [with me].
sentences.i: So I bow down, I prostrate my whole body, and beg your favor, lord, worthy of every praise. The way a father overlooks a son's faults, a friend a friend's, a lover the beloved's — so you, God, should overlook mine.
sentences.n: The three comparisons — pitā iva putrasya, sakhā iva sakhyuḥ, priyaḥ priyāyāḥ — share a single verb, stated only once at the end: arhasi...soḍhum, 'you ought to bear/endure'. Sanskrit regularly compresses parallel clauses this way, letting one verb serve all three. The third pair shifts register: priyaḥ (masc. nom.) and priyāyāḥ (fem. gen.) are 'the [male] beloved' and 'the [female] beloved' — a lover and his beloved — moving the image from father and friend to something more intimate. Praṇamya and praṇidhāya kāyam both describe the same physical prostration, first the general gesture then specifically 'the body' laid down.

sentences.t:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा ।
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे ।
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं ।
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
sentences.tr:
a-dṛṣṭa-pūrvam hṛṣitaḥ asmi dṛṣṭvā |
bhayena ca pravyathitam manaḥ me |
tat eva me darśaya deva rūpam |
prasīda deva-īśa jagat-nivāsa ||

morph.gloss: unseen, not seen (first compound member; negative prefix a- + dṛṣṭa, past participle of dṛś 'to see')
former, previous (a-dṛṣṭa-pūrvam: 'never seen before', acc. sg. neut., object of dṛṣṭvā)
to thrill, be delighted, bristle with joy (hṛṣitaḥ: past participle, nom. sg. masc., 'delighted, thrilled')
to be (asmi: present 1st sg. 'I am'; hṛṣitaḥ + asmi → -aḥ + a- → -o-, elided a marked by avagraha)
to see (dṛṣṭvā: gerund, 'having seen')
fear (instr. sg., 'with fear')
and
to tremble, be agitated, be disturbed (pravyathitam: past participle, nom. sg. neut., agreeing with manas)
mind, heart (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ + m- → -o, visarga sandhi before a voiced consonant)
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'my')
that (acc. sg. neut., object of darśaya, referring to the four-armed form named in the next verse)
indeed, just, very (tat + eva: -t + e- → -d e-, voicing of the final consonant before a vowel)
I (me: enclitic dat. sg. 'to me')
to see (darśaya: causative imperative 2nd sg., 'show!')
god, O God (vocative sg.)
form, shape (acc. sg., object of darśaya)
to be gracious, be favorable (prasīda: imperative 2nd sg. 'be gracious!')
god (first compound member)
lord, ruler (deva-īśa: 'lord of the gods', vocative sg.; -a + ī- → -e-)
the world, universe (first compound member)
dwelling, abode, refuge (jagat-nivāsa: 'O abode of the universe', vocative sg.; -t + n- → -n n-, assimilation)

sentences.l: Having seen [what was] never-seen-before, I am thrilled; and by fear my mind is agitated. That very [form] show me again, O God; be gracious, O lord-of-gods, O abode-of-the-universe.
sentences.i: Having seen what no one has ever seen before, I am overjoyed, but my mind is shaken with fear. Show me that very form again, God; have mercy, lord of the gods, abode of the universe.
sentences.n: Adṛṣṭa-pūrvam, 'not-seen-before', is a common idiom compound: a past participle plus pūrva, 'earlier', meaning 'never before [done]'. The line pairs two opposite feelings in one breath, hṛṣita ('thrilled, bristling with joy') and pravyathita ('shaken, agitated') — Arjuna's vision of the cosmic form in the preceding verses has overwhelmed him with both wonder and terror, and this verse begins his plea to see the gentler form again, completed in 46. Manaḥ shows the ordinary visarga sandhi -aḥ becoming -o before a following voiced consonant (mano me), distinct from the -aḥ + vowel → -o + avagraha pattern seen earlier in this chapter. Deveśa (deva + īśa, 'lord of the gods') and jagannivāsa ('abode of the universe', jagat + nivāsa, with -t assimilating to -n before n-) are both vocatives addressing Kṛṣṇa.

sentences.t:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त- ।
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव ।
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन ।
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥
sentences.tr:
kirīṭinam gadinam cakra-hasta- |
m icchāmi tvām draṣṭum aham tathā eva |
tena eva rūpeṇa catur-bhujena |
sahasra-bāho bhava viśva-mūrte ||

morph.gloss: crowned, wearing a diadem (from kirīṭa 'crown, diadem'; acc. sg. masc., agreeing with tvām, 'you having a diadem')
bearing a mace (from gadā 'mace, club'; acc. sg. masc.)
disc, discus (first compound member)
hand (cakra-hasta: 'having the disc in hand', bahuvrīhi compound describing the form Arjuna wishes to see; the Wikisource print line breaks this compound across the pāda — see note)
hand (m: the final -m of hastam, completing cakra-hastam begun on the previous print line — see note)
to wish, desire (icchāmi: present 1st sg. 'I wish, I desire')
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of draṣṭum)
to see (draṣṭum: infinitive, 'to see', complement of icchāmi)
I (aham: nom. sg. subject of icchāmi; draṣṭum + aham written joined, -m + a- unchanged, the m appearing as anusvāra before the following consonant t- of tathaiva)
thus, so (adverb)
indeed, just, exactly (tathā + eva: -ā + e- → -ai-)
that (tena: instr. sg. masc., 'with that', referring to rūpeṇa)
indeed, just, very (tena + eva: -a + e- → -ai-, cf. tathā + eva above)
form (instr. sg., 'with the ... form')
four (first compound member)
arm (catur-bhuja: 'four-armed', instr. sg. masc., agreeing with rūpeṇa)
thousand (first compound member)
arm (sahasra-bāhu: 'thousand-armed', vocative sg., 'O thousand-armed one')
to be, become (bhava: imperative 2nd sg., 'become, be [again]')
universe, all (first compound member)
form, embodiment, shape (viśva-mūrti: 'universal form, whose form is the universe', vocative sg., 'O universal-formed one')

sentences.l: Crowned, mace-bearing, disc-in-hand — I wish to see you, thus indeed; with that very form, four-armed, O thousand-armed one, become [it], O universal-formed one.
sentences.i: I want to see you as before — with your diadem, your mace, the discus in your hand — in that same four-armed form; become that, thousand-armed one, universal-formed one.
sentences.n: The Wikisource print breaks the compound cakra-hastam ('having the disc in hand') across the line, giving चक्रहस्त- at the end of line 1 and मिच्छामि, 'm' + icchāmi, at the start of line 2 — the leftover final -m of hastam simply begins the next printed word. This is drafted as two words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of ch09 verse 20's सुरेन्द्रलोक-/मश्नन्ति split. Kirīṭin, gadin, and cakra-hasta name the familiar four-armed icon of Viṣṇu — diadem, mace, and discus — the form Arjuna knew before this chapter's terrifying vision, and asks to see again in place of it. The closing address is pointed: Arjuna calls Kṛṣṇa sahasra-bāho, 'thousand-armed', and viśva-mūrte, 'universal-formed' — the very titles of the form that has frightened him — while begging him to 'become' (bhava) the smaller, four-armed shape instead.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)
the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं ।
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् ।
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं ।
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥

mayā prasannena tava arjuna idam |
rūpam param darśitam ātma-yogāt |
tejomayam viśvam anantam ādyam |
yat me tvad anyena na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam ||

morph.gloss: I (mayā: instr. sg. 'by me')
pleased, gracious, favorably disposed (past participle of pra-sad; instr. sg. masc., agreeing with mayā)
you (tava: gen. sg. 'your')
Arjuna, the Pāṇḍava prince Kṛṣṇa is addressing throughout this chapter (vocative 'O Arjuna'; tava + arjuna: a + a → ā)
this (nom./acc. sg. neut., referring to rūpam in the next line; arjuna + idam: a + i → e)
form (acc. sg. neut., object of darśitam)
supreme, highest (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
to see (darśita: causative past participle 'shown, displayed', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
self, own (first compound member)

here 'power, capacity', not the disciplined path named elsewhere (ātma-yoga: 'one's own [supernatural] power', abl. sg. 'through my own power'; darśitam + ātma-yogāt: -m before the vowel ā- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
splendor, radiance, fiery energy (first compound member; -as + m- → -o m-, visarga sandhi of an -as-stem before a voiced consonant)
consisting of, made of (tejo-maya: 'consisting of splendor, blazing', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
universe, all (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
endless, infinite (acc. sg. neut.; viśvam + anantam: -m before the vowel a- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
primal, original, first (acc. sg. neut.; anantam + ādyam: -m before the vowel ā- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
which, that (yat: nom./acc. sg. neut. relative, referring back to rūpam; -t + m- → -n m-, assimilation)
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'of mine')
you (compound stem form of tvam, used in compounds, 'other than you')
other (anyena: instr. sg. masc., agreeing with an unexpressed agent, 'by one other than you'; tvat + anyena: -t + a- → -d a-, voicing before a vowel)
not
to see (dṛṣṭa: past participle 'seen', first compound member)
before, previously (dṛṣṭa-pūrva: 'seen before', nom./acc. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with yat: 'has [never] been seen before')

sentences.l: By me, gracious, this supreme form has been shown to you, Arjuna, through my own power of yoga: blazing, universal, endless, primal — which, by anyone other than you, has never before been seen.
sentences.i: Pleased with you, Arjuna, I have shown you, through my own yogic power, this supreme form — blazing, boundless, without beginning — which no one but you has ever seen before.
sentences.n: The chapter's resolution begins: Kṛṣṇa explains that the vision (rūpam ... darśitam, 'the form has been shown') came through ātma-yogāt, 'my own [power of] yoga' — an unearned gift to Arjuna, not something he attained himself. Ātma-yoga here names Kṛṣṇa's own supernatural capacity, not the disciplined practice yoga usually names elsewhere in the poem. Sandhi: तवार्जुनेदं packs tava + arjuna (a + a → ā) + arjuna + idam (a + i → e); यन्मे is yat + me (-t + m- → -n m-, the same assimilation as tat me → tan me at 1.46).

sentences.t:

र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः ।
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके ।

r na ca kriyābhiḥ na tapobhiḥ ugraiḥ |
evaṃrūpaḥ śakyaḥ aham nṛ-loke |
draṣṭum tvad anyena kuru-pravīra ||
