glossary.व्यपेतभीः: vyapeta-bhīḥ — vyapeta — departed, gone away (past participle of vi-apa-i; first compound member); bhī — fear (vyapeta-bhī: 'whose fear is gone', nom. sg. masc. bahuvrīhi)
glossary.प्रीतमनाः: prīta-manāḥ — prīta — pleased, gladdened (past participle of prī; first compound member); manas — mind (prīta-manas: 'whose mind is glad', nom. sg. masc. bahuvrīhi)
glossary.पुनस्त्वं: punaḥ tvam — punar — again (punaḥ: -aḥ + t- → -as t-, as in duryodhanas tadā at 1.2); tvam — you (nom. sg., subject)
glossary.रूपमिदं: rūpam idam — rūpa — form (acc. sg. neut.); idam — this (acc. sg. neut., in apposition to rūpam; rūpam + idam: -m before the vowel i- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
glossary.प्रपश्य: prapaśya — pra-dṛś/paś — to see, behold (prapaśya: imperative 2nd sg. 'behold!')
glossary.इत्यर्जुनं: iti arjunam — iti — thus (closes the reported speech of vv.47-49; iti + arjunam: -i + a- → -y a-)
glossary.वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा: vāsudevaḥ tathā uktvā — Vāsudeva — 'son of Vasudeva', Kṛṣṇa's patronymic (nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-, as in duryodhanas tadā at 1.2); tathā — thus, in that way (tathā + uktvā: ā + u → o, guṇa); vac — to speak (uktvā: gerund 'having spoken')
glossary.स्वकं: svakam — svaka — one's own (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
glossary.आश्वासयामास: āśvāsayāmāsa — ā-śvas — to take comfort, be reassured (āśvāsayāmāsa: causative periphrastic perfect 3rd sg. 'he comforted, reassured', the same -ām + āsa formation as darśayāmāsa)
glossary.भीतमेनं: bhītam enam — bhīta — frightened (past participle of bhī; acc. sg. masc.); idam/etad — this, he (enam: acc. sg. masc. pronoun, 'him'; bhītam + enam: -m before the vowel e- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
glossary.भूत्वा: bhūtvā — bhū — to become (bhūtvā: gerund 'having become')
glossary.सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा: saumya-vapuḥ mahā-ātmā — saumya — gentle, mild (first compound member); vapus — body, form (saumya-vapus: 'gentle-bodied', nom. sg. masc.; -uḥ + m- → -ur m-, visarga sandhi of a -uḥ ending before a voiced consonant, the same rule as before a vowel, cf. yajur eva at 9.17); mahā — great (first member of a second compound); ātman — self, soul (mahā-ātman: 'great-souled', nom. sg., in apposition to saumya-vapuḥ, both describing Vāsudeva; a + ā → ā)
glossary.दृष्ट्वेदं: dṛṣṭvā idam — dṛś — to see (dṛṣṭvā: gerund 'having seen'; -ā + i- → -e-); idam — this (acc. sg. neut., object of dṛṣṭvā)
glossary.मानुषं: mānuṣam — mānuṣa — human (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
glossary.सौम्यं: saumyam — saumya — gentle, mild (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam)
glossary.जनार्दन: janārdana — Janārdana — 'rouser' or 'tormentor of men', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (vocative)
glossary.इदानीमस्मि: idānīm asmi — idānīm — now (adverb; idānīm + asmi: -m before the vowel a- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
glossary.संवृत्तः: saṃvṛttaḥ — sam-vṛt — to become, turn into, settle (saṃvṛtta: past participle, nom. sg. masc., predicate: 'become, restored')
glossary.सचेताः: sa-cetāḥ — sa — with, possessing (prefix); cetas — mind, consciousness (sa-cetas: 'possessing [normal] consciousness, composed in mind', nom. sg. masc. bahuvrīhi)
glossary.प्रकृतिं: prakṛtim — prakṛti — nature (acc. sg. fem., object of gataḥ, 'gone to [my own] nature')
glossary.गतः: gataḥ — gam — to go (gata: past participle 'gone', nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.सुदुर्दर्शमिदं: su-durdarśam idam — su — very, exceedingly (intensifying prefix); dur — hard, difficult (negative prefix); darśa — seeing, sight (su-dur-darśa: 'very hard to see', from dṛś, acc. sg. neut., agreeing with rūpam); idam — this (acc. sg. neut., in apposition; su-durdarśam + idam: -m before the vowel i- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
glossary.दृष्टवानसि: dṛṣṭavān asi — dṛś — to see (dṛṣṭavān: perfect active participle 'having seen', nom. sg. masc.; joined with the following auxiliary without change, as bhagavān uvāca is written joined); as — to be (asi: present 2nd sg. 'you are'; together, dṛṣṭavān asi is a periphrastic perfect, 'you have seen')
glossary.यन्मम: yat mama — yad — which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring to rūpam; -t + m- → -n m-, as in yan me at v.47); aham — I (mama: gen. sg. 'my, of mine')
glossary.देवा: devāḥ — deva — god, deity (nom. pl., subject; the visarga of an -āḥ ending simply drops before a following vowel, with no merger — unlike the -aḥ-before-a rule seen with śakya in v.48, this -āḥ form just loses its visarga, cf. purūṣā dharmasyāsya at 9.3)
glossary.अप्यस्य: api asya — api — even, also (api + asya: -i + a- → -y a-); idam — this (asya: gen. sg. neut., 'of this [form]')
glossary.दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः: darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ — darśana — sight, seeing, beholding (first compound member); kāṅkṣin — desiring, longing for (darśana-kāṅkṣin: 'longing to see', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.नाहं: na aham — na — not (na + aham: a + a → ā); aham — I (nom. sg., subject)
glossary.वेदैर्न: vedaiḥ na — veda — the Veda (vedaiḥ: instr. pl. 'by the Vedas'; -aiḥ + n- → -air n-, as in vedayajñādhyayanaiḥ na at v.48); na — not
glossary.चेज्यया: ca ijyayā — ca — and (ca + ijyayā: a + i → e); ijyā — sacrifice, worship (instr. sg.)
glossary.एवंविधो: evaṃvidhaḥ — evam — thus, such (first compound member); vidha — kind, manner (evaṃ-vidha: 'of this kind', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before d- → -o)
glossary.त्वनन्यया: tu ananyayā — tu — but (tu + ananyayā: u + a → va, yaṇ sandhi); an-anya — not other, undivided, exclusive (ananyayā: instr. sg. fem., agreeing with bhaktyā)
glossary.अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन: aham evaṃvidhaḥ arjuna — aham — I (nom. sg., subject; aham + evaṃvidhaḥ: -m before the vowel e- simply written joined, no phonetic change); evam — thus, such (first compound member); vidha — kind, manner (evaṃ-vidha: 'of this kind', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha, the regular pattern); Arjuna — Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.तत्त्वेन: tattvena — tattva — true nature, reality, essence (instr. sg. 'in [my true] reality, in truth')
glossary.प्रवेष्टुं: praveṣṭum — pra-viś — to enter into (praveṣṭum: infinitive)
glossary.परंतप: parantapa — Parantapa — 'scorcher of the foe', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो: mat-karma-kṛt mat-paramaḥ — mad — me, my (compound stem form of aham; devoices to mat- before a voiceless consonant, here k-, contrast the voiced mad-bhaktaḥ just below where it stands before the voiced bh-); karman — action, work (second member); kṛt — doer, agent (from kṛ; mat-karma-kṛt: 'one who does my work', nom. sg. masc.; kṛt + mat-: -t + m- → -n m-, assimilation); mad — me (compound stem, again devoicing to mat- before the voiceless p- of parama); parama — supreme (mat-parama: 'having me as the highest [goal]', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
glossary.मद्भक्तः: mad-bhaktaḥ — mad — me, my (compound stem, here unchanged before the voiced bh-); bhakta — devotee (mad-bhakta: 'my devotee', nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.सङ्गवर्जितः: saṅga-varjitaḥ — saṅga — attachment, clinging (from sañj, 'to cling'; first compound member); varjita — devoid of, free from (past participle of vṛj 'to exclude'; saṅga-varjita: 'free from attachment', nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.निर्वैरः: nirvairaḥ — nir — without, free from (negative prefix); vaira — hostility, enmity (nirvaira: 'free from hostility', nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.सर्वभूतेषु: sarva-bhūteṣu — sarva — all (first compound member); bhūta — being (sarva-bhūta: 'all beings', loc. pl. 'toward all beings')
glossary.यः: yaḥ — yad — who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative)
glossary.मामेति: mām eti — aham — I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'); i — to go, come, attain (eti: present 3rd sg. 'goes, attains'; mām + eti: -m before the vowel e- simply written joined, no phonetic change)
glossary.पाण्डव: pāṇḍava — Pāṇḍava — 'son of Pāṇḍu', addressed to Arjuna (vocative)

about: Chapter 11, the Vision of the Cosmic Form (Viśvarūpadarśanayoga), is the poem's central theophany. Arjuna, having heard Kṛṣṇa teach on manifestation and devotion, asks to see Kṛṣṇa's true, universal form if it can be seen; Kṛṣṇa grants him a divine eye and reveals a form of overwhelming, terrifying majesty, blazing like a thousand suns at once, countless mouths and eyes and arms containing the whole universe within it. Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies rushing into those flaming mouths to their deaths, and Kṛṣṇa names himself Time, the destroyer of worlds, come to annihilate them all whether or not Arjuna fights. Shaken and afraid, Arjuna offers a long hymn of apology and awe, asking pardon for every past familiarity and begging Kṛṣṇa to return to his gentler, four-armed and finally human form. The chapter closes as Kṛṣṇa complies and states its resolution: this form cannot be reached by Vedic study, sacrifice, austerity or gift-giving, but only through single-minded devotion, and that whoever acts for Kṛṣṇa, holds him as the highest goal, is devoted to him, free of attachment and without hostility to any being, attains him. With that promise the episode ends, and the poem turns next to devotion itself as a path in its own right.
